decisions.reason: This trend-driven devore line has had three seasons to show its value, but it has several variants, the firm promises reorder continuity, and stocking it costs little in an existing warehouse, so keeping the option is still worthwhile.
This transparent burnout line is fashion-dependent and could be rotated out, but it sits close to the core collection and costs little to carry, so the firm likely keeps it while demand persists.

As a single burnout article that overlaps with Products A and B, it is the most likely of the decorative fabrics to be retired in a collection refresh, but with no sign of failure, keeping it remains the cheaper choice.
Velour-like upholstery fabric is a durable segment where ongoing demand is plausible, and carrying the article costs little.
Flame-retardant plain fabrics are staple articles needed for contract and retail buyers, with steady demand and low carrying cost.
Polyester satin lining is a basic complement to the sewing and made-to-measure service and is unlikely to be dropped.
